prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit. Create one landscape production repair atlas with a THREE-column TWO-row grid but exactly FIVE circular tokens. The top row has three circles; the bottom row has two circles at left and centre. The entire BOTTOM-RIGHT cell is EMPTY TRANSPARENT SPACE: no sixth circle, rim, blank disk, placeholder, motif or duplicate. Every occupied cell is an equal square, and every circle is centered in it at 80 percent of the cell width.

REFERENCE 1 is icons-08; REFERENCE 2 is icons-09; REFERENCE 3 is icons-05. All source atlases have five columns and four rows. References 1 and 2 supply the specified edit targets; reference 3 supplies the established small-mammal ancestor. Preserve the established token compositions except for the corrections below. Do not reproduce the full sheets or add their other subjects.

Use the same luminous opaque gouache and selective fine ink, textured deep lapis interiors, jade, burnt ochre, muted coral and ivory highlights, very narrow ivory-gold rims, strong simplified silhouettes legible at 64px, opaque painted circular interiors and fully transparent exterior with generous gutters. No text, labels, letters, numbers, grid lines, watermark, modern equipment or shadows outside circles.

CRITICAL IDENTITY: the social family is furred long-tailed TREE-DWELLING ANIMALS, not people in clothes. The three small-mammal subjects are all descendants of the pointed-snouted, round-eared, LONG-SLENDER-TAILED ancestor: coats may be thin or thick soft fur, never quills, hedgehog bodies or missing tails. CRITICAL TIDE MEANING: full Moon versus quarter Moon compares the vertical distance between HIGH and LOW static water levels at an identical shore, never larger versus smaller surf waves.

Exact occupied-cell order, left to right and top to bottom:

CELL 1, TOP LEFT, Social group. Edit REFERENCE 2 row 1 column 1, using the established TREE DWELLERS in REFERENCE 1 row 1 column 1 as the animal identity anchor. Replace every human and clothed figure with those SAME FURRED LONG-TAILED PRIMATES. Four animals of related body shape share branches: one gently grooms another, one watches outward, and a juvenile stays close. Their bodies are covered in ochre fur, with recognizable primate faces, grasping hands/feet and long curling tails. Show care and shared vigilance, not a human family living in a tree. No clothing, loincloth, woven wrap, tools or human faces. Target subject: Four established ochre-furred, long-tailed tree dwellers share a sheltered branch network as an animal family: one grooms a companion, another keeps watch and a smaller juvenile stays close. Preserve their primate faces, grasping hands and feet, full body fur and visibly curling tails; there are no humans, clothes or tools.

CELL 2, TOP CENTRE, Varied survivors. Edit REFERENCE 1 row 2 column 5, with SMALL FURRED ANIMALS in REFERENCE 3 row 4 column 5 as the ancestor anchor. Four animals retain the ancestor's pointed shrew-like snout, round ears, low four-legged body and LONG SLENDER TAIL, clearly visible extending well beyond the rump. Vary only the already present coats: thin, medium, thick and softly shaggy. Thick coats must read as soft flowing fur, NEVER stiff spines, quills, hedgehog domes or porcupines. Do not shorten, conceal or omit the tails. Preserve the neutral ground and comparative group arrangement. Target subject: Four members of the established small shrew-like mammal lineage stand together on neutral ground, each retaining a pointed snout, round ears, a low four-legged body and a visibly long slender tail extending beyond its rump. Their coats vary from thin through dense to softly shaggy while the body plan stays the same; thick fur has no quills, spikes or hedgehog dome.

CELL 3, TOP RIGHT, Cold-adapted populations. Edit REFERENCE 1 row 3 column 1, with the SAME ancestor from REFERENCE 3 row 4 column 5. Keep snow, rocks, two adults and a smaller juvenile, but replace the quilled hedgehog-like bodies with softly thick-furred SHREW-LIKE MAMMALS. Every animal has a pointed snout, round visible ears and a clearly LONG SLENDER TAIL emerging from the fur and extending beyond the body. Thick fur follows the body rather than forming a spiny dome. No quills, no spikes, no short-tail animal substitution, no extra species. Target subject: Three thick-soft-furred descendants of the same shrew-like mammals forage beside snow and low sheltering rocks, including one smaller juvenile. All retain clearly pointed snouts, round ears and visibly long slender tails beyond their thick coats, without quills, spikes, hedgehog bodies or short hidden tails.

CELL 4, BOTTOM LEFT, Surviving lineages. Edit REFERENCE 1 row 3 column 2, with the SAME ancestor from REFERENCE 3 row 4 column 5. Preserve the paired warm-refuge and snowy-habitat composition separated by a natural rock ridge. In the warm green spring setting, a thin-furred adult and juvenile; in the snow setting, thick-soft-furred relatives and a juvenile. All visibly share POINTED SHREW-LIKE SNOUTS, ROUND EARS and LONG SLENDER TAILS well beyond their rumps. Keep the difference in coat thickness and setting, not different species silhouettes. No hedgehog bodies, quills, spines or shortened/hidden tails. Target subject: Two small family groups occupy adjoining habitats divided by a rock ridge: thin-furred shrew-like mammals beside a green spring and thick-soft-furred relatives beside lingering snow, each with a juvenile. Every individual retains the same pointed snout, round ears and conspicuous long slender tail, making related lineages visible across the two settings without quills or hedgehog anatomy.

CELL 5, BOTTOM CENTRE, Lunar rhythm. Edit REFERENCE 2 row 2 column 3. Replace the wave-height comparison with two stacked calm shoreline diagrams, equal size and IDENTICAL HOOKED SHORE PROFILE and rock-face geometry. Upper diagram: a FULL circular pale Moon and EXACTLY TWO static horizontal water-level traces against the rock face, one high and one low, WIDELY separated. Lower diagram: a QUARTER Moon with exactly HALF its circular disk illuminated and EXACTLY TWO static horizontal water-level traces against the same rock face, closely spaced around the same middle height. In each diagram the two traces themselves represent high and low water; do not add a third middle waterline. Use a thin translucent jade wash between the paired levels if helpful. The land profile and scale must match so the vertical separation alone shows broad versus narrow HIGH-TO-LOW TIDAL RANGE. Water is flat and calm in both; no breakers, surf, crests, storms or wave-amplitude encoding. No arrows, letters, numbers or labels. Preserve the pale Moon identity and restrained paired craters where visible; no four-phase sequence crowded over unrelated shore strips. Target subject: Two matching views of the same hooked shore profile show calm water beneath a full Moon in the upper view and a quarter Moon with exactly half its disk lit in the lower view. Each view contains exactly two clear static horizontal water-level marks against the same rock face: widely separated high and low levels for the full Moon, closely spaced high and low levels for the quarter Moon; no surf or wave-height difference carries the comparison.

CELL 6, BOTTOM RIGHT: leave completely transparent and empty. Final atlas contains exactly FIVE finished circular icons. All tails remain visibly long, every animal coat is fur rather than spines, no humans or clothes appear, and the tide icon uses two flat water-level marks per shore diagram with wide versus narrow spacing.
